title: Whose Indicators? A Plural-Values Framework for the Co-Design of Urban Observatories
content: Urban observatories support evidence-based planning yet less attention has been paid to whose values their indicators reflect and who decides what should be measured. This paper examines how decision-making authority is distributed within observatories and how plural values can be incorporated without sacrificing comparability. A six-dimensional coding matrix is applied to public documentation from 24 urban observatories while 8 community-led monitoring initiatives are examined as institutional precedents. The analysis reveals a consistent gap between stated commitments to inclusion and the forms of participation built into observatory governance. Decisions about indicator ownership, knowledge selection and review remain controlled by host institutions. However, community-led initiatives show that values can be elicited, translated into indicators and used accountably. These findings inform a Plural-Values Framework organized around three stages: eliciting diverse and potentially conflicting values, co-producing candidate indicators through transdisciplinary deliberation, and integrating them through multi-criteria and mixed-method evaluation. Governance and periodic review operate across all three stages. The framework retains the comparable indicators required by the Urban Monitoring Framework and SDG 11 while allowing communities to develop locally governed measures. It offers observatories an institutional design for combining comparability with community authority and locally grounded knowledge.
